messages:
sasha: noticing persistent p95 token-generation latency on a subset of Dedicated slices in eu-west, correlating with egress spikes. not full OOMs, just tail spikes.
leo: ack. which pools? any tenant patterns?
sasha: affected pools: ded-eu-west-03 / ded-eu-west-04. tenants: mix of small steady and one big interactive. egress bytes jump ~3x during spikes.
infra-bot: [alert] egress-queue-depth high on ded-eu-west-03 between 15:24-15:39 UTC. rate-limited flows observed.
olivia: sounds like noisy-neighbor egress hogging. did we hit the nic shaper limits?
maria: checking node telemetry... TX queue full, interrupts rising. NIC shaping configured at 10Gbps per slice, but observed effective throughput >12Gbps due to PCI bursts.
dave: temporary mitigation: can we move the big interactive tenant to a separate dedicated slice or soft-quota them?
sasha: yes temporary plan: manual routing override to pool ded-eu-west-06. need rollout window and traffic drain plan.
nashley: we should avoid manual for long — prefer dynamic routing fallback by egress pressure. but need a quick fix now.
leo: who's oncall for prod?
prod-oncall: i'm here. can we do a canary move for 5% of traffic first? watch p95 + egress.
sasha: will kick off a partial re-route. command: `routerctl route --tenant tenant-id-42 --from ded-eu-west-03 --to ded-eu-west-06 --percent 5`
maria: grabbing logs and KV cache hit rates. if we move only interactive frontends we should not thrash caches too much.
dave: i'll pre-create a soft-cap for tenant-id-42 on ded-eu-west-06 at 80% capacity to avoid overcommit: `poolctl set-capacity ded-eu-west-06 tenant-id-42 0.8`
infra-bot: [action] scheduled route change job 3344 by sasha. will report status.
leo: after partial move, can we enable egress-aware scoring on router? Rule idea: prefer pools with <75% egress utilization when routing high-rt tenants.
olivia: that scoring rule exists but was disabled for dedicated slices in last rollout because it increased evictions. we can re-enable with backoff threshold.
nashley: long-term we should: 1) add per-tenant egress reservations for interactive workloads, 2) surface token-level egress costs to console, 3) improve NIC firmware rate reporting.
maria: cost note: moving traffic increases inter-AZ egress in some cases — watch billing for next cycle.
prod-oncall: partial routing completed, 5% shifted. initial p95 improvement -3% at 1m.
sasha: ok continue ramp to 30% over 10m if metrics stable.
dave: ramping. also enabling `egress_shield` config on target pool to drop large sustained flows rather than letting them hog queues. config snippet:
```
pool:
  name: ded-eu-west-06
  egress_shield: true
  shield_threshold_mbps: 6000
  shield_backoff_s: 30
```
leo: nice. can we add a soft-fallback to quantized model variant when backend latency >300ms so we avoid user-visible timeouts?
nashley: yes thats separate but low-effort. add a route policy: `if p95 > 300ms -> route variant:q8-lowlat`
maria: logs show one node in ded-eu-west-03 with sustained PCIe DMA bursts; opening hardware ticket but may take days.
sasha: summarize actions: (1) ramp partial route -> 30% (dave), (2) enable egress_shield on target (dave), (3) re-enable egress-aware scoring with backoff (leo), (4) open HW ticket (maria), (5) monitor cost impact (ashley).
prod-oncall: will keep watch, alert if p95 regresses or egress costs spike >10% baseline.
leo: followup — we should add a small internal experiment to measure how KV cache cold misses affect p95 when we migrate — assign to olivia.
olivia: on it, will run a synthetic traffic test tonight.
sasha: thanks everyone. will post post-mortem if this persists. :thumbsup:
